data: Qualitative Methods: Researching the Social, Political and the Historical

This course introduces the students to the various aspects, approaches and techniques of qualitative research. Qualitative research in social studies is significant for theory building and examining empiricism through exploration of the field. Distinct from quantitative methods, qualitative research methods involve close and long-standing interaction with the participants leading to various ethical and subjective considerations in research. This is also implicated in the researcher’s own location on and off the field. In addition, conducting field work involves multiple stages, sample selections, approaching and entering the field and planned process of observation. In the light of this, the course is divided into four sections. First section “Overview: key concepts and definitions” addresses the fundamental concepts related to qualitative research and the subject of methodological awareness required for conducting qualitative research. In the second module, “Various approaches of qualitative research”, the course offers detailed discussions on ethnography, case studies, life history method content and discourse analyses and the stages of theory building following an inductive approach to research. This module also extensively discusses the structural challenges and possibilities of conducting field work. The third module “Political economy of qualitative research” engages with the broad questions of how to conduct auto-ethnography and use the self as a research method; it deals with concepts like cultural insider, covert research etc. The fourth and the last module “Research Project” includes empirical research projects conducted by the students following various stages of qualitative research.
